chunks: And whatever is in it from Ali ibn Hassan, I have narrated it from Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan - may Allah be pleased with him - from Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan Al-Saffar, from Ali ibn Hassan Al-Wasiti; and I have narrated it from my father - may Allah be pleased with him - from Sa'd ibn Abdullah, from Al-Hasan ibn Musa Al-Khashshab, from Ali ibn Hassan Al-Wasiti.

key_terms.رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ: May Allah be pleased with him (honorific for narrators)

ai.seo_question: How is the narration from Ali ibn Hassan transmitted in this text?
ai.summary: This passage exemplifies the rigorous methodology of hadith verification (tahqiq) employed by Shaykh al-Saduq, emphasizing the reliability of his direct teachers—Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan Al-Saffar and his father, Sa'd ibn Abdullah—to authenticate the narrations of Ali ibn Hassan Al-Wasiti. By explicitly stating 'I narrated' (roytu), the author establishes a personal chain of custody, reinforcing the authenticity of the transmission within the Shia scholarly tradition.
